Facetious

fuh-SEE-shuhs · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Facetious is joking about serious matters in a way that is inappropriate or unwelcome.

He couldn't resist a facetious aside about the fire drill, even though his supervisor was standing right there.

Worked Example

Asked why the bridge had collapsed, the engineer's facetious reply -- 'gravity, mostly' -- did not go over well with the investigators.

The moment called for a serious answer, and his joke, however clever, was facetious because it made light of something that deserved a real response.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

flippant: not showing a serious or respectful attitude

glib: fluent but insincere or shallow, often joking

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

solemn: serious and dignified

earnest: sincere and serious in intention

Where it sits · how disrespectful the joking is — playful → facetious → mocking

playful vs. facetious: Playful is milder than facetious: playful joking is lighthearted fun with no real disrespect, while facetious remarks push harder, joking about serious matters where humor is not welcome.

mocking vs. facetious: Mocking is harsher than facetious: a facetious comment jokes inappropriately about something serious, but mockery goes further, openly ridiculing a person with real contempt.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — facet- (facetus)

root — facet- (facetus): witty, elegant, urbane -- unrelated to the everyday word 'facet' (as in a gem's facet), which comes from a different root (Latin facetus)

suffix — -ious

suffix — -ious: possessing the quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Facetious comes from Latin facetus, 'witty or urbane,' plus -ious. Its root doesn't survive as a common modern English word on its own -- and importantly, it is not related to the everyday word 'facet,' despite the resemblance; that word comes from an entirely different French root meaning 'little face.'

Use the root in a new word: facetiae

Use the root in a new word: facetiae: The professor's collected facetiae, published after his death, revealed a much funnier man than his stern lectures ever suggested.

Word Building

Word Choice

Facetious always carries a hint of disapproval -- it's joking at the wrong moment, not just joking in general. Watch the trap: the everyday word 'facet' (as in a diamond's facet) looks related but comes from a completely different root.
